tested_scope_delta.overlap: Both policies preserve the same core safety invariant that a fresh current snapshot is not rollback authority while an older writer can still cross an irreversible boundary, and both avoid the unsafe rollback pattern exhibited by current_min within the tested lattice.
tested_scope_delta.separation: Their action semantics and measured behavior descriptors are materially different. wait_then_min explicitly consumes a wait/settle action before re-planning; this produces substantially higher tested terminal coverage and lower irreversible-C retry exposure than forward_guard, but at materially higher expected action/latency cost. forward_guard instead actively reconciles forward without first waiting, reducing expected action cost but giving up tested coverage and increasing irreversible retry exposure. Thus wait_then_min is not merely a delayed spelling of forward_guard and forward_guard is not a strict substitute for wait_then_min across the archive descriptors.
tested_scope_delta.pareto_relationship: At budget 2, wait_then_min improves terminal coverage (65.91% vs 47.73%) and irreversible-C retry exposure (0.1023 vs 0.1932) relative to forward_guard, while forward_guard improves expected incremental action cost (0.3636 vs 0.6364). Neither dominates across all three behavior axes. The source explicitly frames these as separate safe policy niches in a behavior-indexed archive selected by objective/preference.
